senses.gloss:
Śleṣman means generally that with which parts of a thing are joined together (from śliṣ, ‘join’): with reference to a hide, ‘laces’ of some sort may be intended; to a chariot, ‘bonds’ or ‘cords’ are probably meant; and to wood, ‘glue’ is perhaps the sense.
Foot notes aitareya brāhmaṇa, v. 32, 6; Jaiminīya Upanisad brāhmaṇa, iii. 17, 3; Chāndogya upaniṣad, iv. 17, 4.
kāṭhaka Saṃhitā, xxxiv. 9. Cf. pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa, xvi. 1, 13, where a chariot (ratha) is called śleṣmavant, ‘tied with ropes.’
kauṣītaki brāhmaṇa, vi. 12. Cf. the Upaniṣads, cited in n. 1, and Sāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka, ii. 1, which looks like a bad secondary version of the passage in the Jaiminīya.
